articles.title: Tech Titans Join Trump to Fete China’s Xi at Lavish State Dinner
articles.summary: Luminaries from Wall Street and Silicon Valley joined President Donald Trump for a state dinner honoring his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, in a demonstrati...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Luminaries from Wall Street and Silicon Valley joined President Donald Trump for a state dinner honoring his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, in a demonstration of US technological and financial might.

Trump has welcomed Xi with fanfare this week, affording rare state visit honors to a counterpart considered one of America's biggest industrial and military rivals. The race to dominate in artificial intelligence has emerged as a growing flashpoint, with Chinese companies rapidly closing the gap with US models.

Even as they compete, both governments are agreed on pushing ahead with AI's development despite mounting concerns over the technology's impact on jobs, the environment and even the future of humanity.

Thursday's dinner brought together some of the most influential names in that sphere. Among those invited were Nvidia Corp.'s Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman. Tech icons Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk and Tim Cook were among those with coveted invites, as well as Satya Nadella of Microsoft Corp. and Sundar Pichai of Google's parent, Alphabet Inc.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other top Trump advisers on trade and the economy, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Energy Secretary Chris Wright and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, were on the guest list, as was Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh.

Trump's warm welcome for Xi, however, has also drawn criticism, including from a Republican senator, Roger Wicker of Mississippi, who questioned the administration's decision to salute China's leader. As guests arrived on Thursday, protesters near the White House could be heard chanting, including calls to "Free Hong Kong" and "Free Tibet."

Trump and first lady Melania Trump welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan. The US first lady wore what appeared to be a white top with a large bow and black pants, while Madame Peng wore a red long-sleeved dress.

Finance executives on the guest list for the evening included Jane Fraser of Citigroup Inc., Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase & Co., Stephen Schwarzman of Blackstone Inc., David Solomon of Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Mastercard Inc.'s Michael Miebach. Other business titans invited included Kelly Ortberg of Boeing Co. and David Ellison of Paramount Skydance Corp.

articles.title: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic may launch AI safety standard by early 2027
articles.summary: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027,
articles.body: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027, a report from The Information has claimed, adding that they have reached out to former White House AI policy advisor Sriram Krishnan to serve as chief executive. The report says that the planned organisation, provisionally named the Standards Authority for Frontier AI (SAFA), will operate independently of government administration. Its primary mission will be to define practical benchmarks for the three companies' public safety pledges and provide direct support to developers evaluating cutting-edge models prior to commercial deployment.Citing people familiar with the initiative, the report said that apart from Krishnan, the companies have reached out to Arati Prabhakar, former director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, to take the top post at SAFA. The three technology giants are also weighing whether SAFA should conduct direct model assessments in-house.While the United States Center for AI Standards and Innovation already handles federal evaluation, insiders noted persistent concerns that the government agency lacks adequate technical and financial resources to thoroughly inspect complex frontier systems.Momentum builds following safety proposalsThe push toward a joint authority follows weeks of escalating industry dialogue. About 10 days ago, an OpenAI spokesperson confirmed to CNBC that the company was holding active talks with Google and Anthropic regarding coordinated safety frameworks. These discussions gained momentum following a proposal published on X in July by Sir Demis Hassabis, co-founder of Google DeepMind and Alphabet’s chief scientist. Hassabis argued for a US-backed standards body modeled after a public-private partnership or a self-regulatory watchdog, drawing comparisons to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).While Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI remain locked in a race for commercial dominance, leadership across all three firms has faced mounting scrutiny over potential catastrophic and security risks. The momentum toward collective oversight accelerated earlier this month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei released an essay calling for an industrywide slowdown in the release of frontier models to allow safety mechanisms to catch up.You use AI every day. articles.title: Australia Demands More AI Safeguards After Revealing OpenAI Hack
articles.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used his trip to the United Nations to call for greater controls on artificial intelligence, pointing to the revel...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese used his trip to the United Nations to call for greater controls on artificial intelligence, pointing to the revelation that OpenAI had hacked a government website as evidence of the need for tougher safeguards.

"Recently, an artificial intelligence agent infiltrated an Australian government website. This is unacceptable and it is why Australia has been leading the way in establishing Australian standards for AI," Albanese said in New York, adding that countries needed to work together to shape how the technology develops.

Listen and follow The Bloomberg Australia Podcast on Apple, Spotify, YouTube or wherever you get your podcasts.

The minister in charge of AI policy, Andrew Charlton, told national broadcaster ABC that the OpenAI breach "makes the case" for the government's safety goals, adding that he aimed to pass new laws early next year on AI safety and data center construction. The measures would seek to manage risks highlighted by the June hack of a government website, he said.

While the intrusion into a government health-statistics website was minor, the incident underscored the risk that AI models can circumvent security barriers without human control. Albanese and other ministers have also criticized how long OpenAI took to notify Canberra, with almost three months elapsing between the breach and the company sending notice to a generic government email address.
